issue.title: v5.1.5 breaks coverage whitelist include directory globbing
issue.body:
hi,

v5.1.5 of phpunit breaks coverage whitelist include globbing

``` xml
    <filter>
        <whitelist processUncoveredFilesFromWhitelist="true" addUncoveredFilesFromWhitelist="true">
            <directory suffix=".php">./bundles/*/src</directory>
        </whitelist>
    </filter>
```

git bisect shows commit 55cca0f707e0db4a069473d7394bf2f08df33b83 as the culprit.

An is_dir check is introduces before any wildcard expansion takes place, thus always failing.

thanks
vkunz

``` xml
  <filter>
  <whitelist processUncoveredFilesFromWhitelist="true">
    <directory suffix="Test.php">/tests/src/</directory>
  </whitelist>
</filter>

</phpunit>
```

then i execute

``` shell
phpunit -v -c tests/phpunitxml --coverage-clover tests/reports/coverage.xml tests
```

then i receive

```
No whitelist configured, no code coverage will be generated
```

please, how can i do fix this?

Thanks!
you should whitelist files which contain logic (which you want to test, not your test files), your whitelist should be `<directory suffix=".php">./src/</directory>`

Probably I made some mistake on my paths!

Anyway, thank you for the help!

I got this error with a misconfigured directory within whitelist. Maybe it's just a matter of inappropriate wording of the error message.
I fixed it! As @elmar-hinz said, it was a misconfigured path. The thing to remember is to make sure the path in whitelist is relative to the phpunit.xml file! D'oh. Sounds obvious now :D
@elmar-hinz Yeah, I guess would be nice if the message was something like "invalid whitelist path" or something, rather than "no whitelist configured" but oh well :)

issue.title: Added more descriptive error messages for whitelist issues
issue.body:
ref: issue #2049 
The "No white list configured" was misleading when you had a whitelist element configured in `phpunit.xml`, but using invalid directories so that no test files were returned. Added a check for the existence of the white list element, and moved the original error to there. Then updated the "empty" error message to more accurately note the problem.

rename.from: "No whitelist configured" error when directory doesn't exist
rename.to: Misleading error message when whitelist configuration contains paths that do not exist
